readout_other: Whole-cell patch clamp (sAP, iAP, sEPSC, mEPSC); Fura-2 cytosolic Ca2+ imaging
direction_notes: About two-thirds of neurons increased sAP firing and sEPSC frequency with continuous SAW US (immediate or delayed responders); the rest did not respond. Effects depended on extracellular Ca2+ and L-type channels; no change at 400 mW/cm2.

exposures.label: SAW ultrasound chip, cultured rat hippocampal neurons, 7.65, 11.87 and 15.88 MHz

device.model: SAW US neuromodulation chip, interdigital transducers on LiTaO3

timing.protocol_description: Continuous standing SAW US; 60-s sessions at 120-s intervals at increasing Ispta (0, 25, 50, 100, 400 mW/cm2) for each frequency; later experiments used 2-min stimulation at 100 mW/cm2 within a 20-min recording.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: To investigate the efect of US stimulation on neural excitability with high temporal resolution, we designed and fabricated three SAW US neuromodulation chips based on the work of Lin et al. [9] using lithium tantalate $( \mathrm { L i T a O } _ { 3 } )$ wafers with resonant frequencies of 7.65, 11.87, and 15.88 MHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: We applied US stimulation at increasing $I _ { S P T A }$ ranging from 25 to 400 $\mathrm { m W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ at each of the three selected frequencies (Fig. 2A).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Subsequently, we applied a series of 60-s continuous US stimulation sessions at 120-s intervals (Fig. 2A).

flags.reason: Ispta measured by laser Doppler velocimetry on the chip, in mW/cm2 (0 to 400); converted to W/cm2; domain not a water or in-situ statement.
